discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / ultracold quantum gases
motivation: Zoller and co-workers proposed in 1998 that ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise the Bose-Hubbard model with fully tunable parameters. Bloch and Greiner then observed the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator quantum phase transition (Nature 2002), the first clean realisation of a paradigmatic strongly correlated phase transition in a controllable quantum system. This turned Feynman's idea of a quantum simulator into a working experimental method. Bloch and Greiner later developed quantum gas microscopes that image and address single atoms at single lattice sites, revealing antiferromagnetic correlations in the Fermi-Hubbard model, string order, entanglement entropy and many-body localisation. Zoller's theoretical framework, which also covers lattice gauge theories and Rydberg-atom architectures, guided the field. Together their work founded analog quantum simulation, now a central tool of condensed-matter physics and quantum technology, and it answers long-standing questions that conventional materials could not settle.
